verses.21:14: And the Lord gave death in Israel, and seventy thousand men fell from Israel.
verses.21:15: And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. And as he was destroying, the Lord saw and relented concerning the calamity, and said to the angel who was destroying, "Let it be enough for you; hold back your hand." And the angel of the Lord was standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:16: And David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between the earth and heaven, and his sword was drawn in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem; and David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on their faces.
verses.21:17: And David said to God, "Was it not I who said to number the people? And I am the one who sinned; I have indeed done evil. But these sheep, what have they done? Lord God, let Your hand be upon me and upon the house of my father, and not upon Your people for destruction, Lord."
verses.21:18: And the angel of the Lord told Gad to say to David that he should go up to set up an altar to the Lord at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:19: And David went up according to the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the Lord.
verses.21:20: And Ornan turned and saw the king and his four sons with him, methachabein; and Ornan was threshing wheat.
verses.21:21: And David came to Ornan, and Ornan came out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
verses.21:22: And David said to Ornan, "Give me your place of the threshing floor, and I will build on it an altar to the Lord; for silver of full worth give it to me, and the plague will cease from the people."
verses.21:23: And Ornan said to David, "Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good before him; look, I have given the calves for a burnt offering, and the plow for wood, and the grain for a sacrifice; I have given everything."
verses.21:24: And King David said to Ornan, "No, for I will surely buy it for silver of full worth; for I will by no means take what belongs to you for the Lord, to offer up a burnt offering without cost to the Lord."
verses.21:25: And David gave Ornan for his place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
verses.21:26: And David built there an altar to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings and offerings of deliverance; and he cried out to the Lord, and He answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering, and consumed the burnt offering.
verses.21:27: And the Lord spoke to the angel, and he put the sword away into the sheath.
verses.21:28: At that time, when David saw that He had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
verses.21:29: Now the tent of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time in Bamoth in Gibeon.
verses.21:30: And David was not able to go before it to seek God, because he did not hasten from before the sword of the angel of the Lord.
verses.22:1: And David said, "This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for burnt offering for Israel."
verses.22:2: And David said to gather all the proselytes in the land of Israel; and he appointed stonecutters to cut dressed stones to build a house for God.
verses.22:3: And David prepared much iron for the nails of the doors and of the gates and for the hinges, and bronze in abundance; there was no weighing it.
verses.22:4: And for cedar timbers, there was no number; for the Sidonians and the Tyrians were bringing cedar timbers in abundance to David.
verses.22:5: And David said, "Solomon my son is a tender young boy, and the house to be built for the Lord is to be for greatness above, for a name and for glory throughout all the earth; I will prepare for it." And David prepared in abundance before his death.
verses.22:6: And he called Solomon his son and commanded him to build the house for the Lord God of Israel.
verses.22:7: And David said to Solomon, "Child, it was upon my soul to build a house for the name of the Lord God.
verses.22:8: And a word of the Lord came to me, saying, 'You have shed blood in abundance, and you have made great wars; you shall not build a house for My name, because you have shed much blood upon the earth before Me.
verses.22:9: Look, a son is being born to you; he will be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all the enemies around, for Solomon is his name, and I will give peace and quiet upon Israel in his days.
verses.22:10: He will build a house for My name, and he will be to Me as a son, and I to him as a father, and I will set upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.'
verses.22:11: And now, son, the Lord will be with you, and He will grant success, and you will build a house for the Lord your God, as He spoke concerning you.
verses.22:12: Only may the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, both to keep and to do the law of the Lord your God.
verses.22:13: Then He will grant success if you take care to do the statutes and the judgments that the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be courageous and be strong; do not fear and do not be terrified.
verses.22:14: And look, according to my poverty I have prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold, and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron of which there is no weighing, because it is in abundance; and timbers and stones I have prepared, and add to these.
verses.22:15: And with you, add an abundance of those who do work: craftsmen and builders of stone and carpenters of wood, and every skilled person in every work,
verses.22:16: in gold, in silver, in bronze, and in iron, there is no number. Arise and act, and may the Lord be with you."
verses.22:17: And David commanded the servants, the leaders of Israel, to help Solomon his son:
verses.22:18: "Is not the Lord with you? And He has given you rest all around, for He has given the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and the land has been subdued before the Lord and before His people.
verses.22:19: Now give your hearts and your souls to seek the Lord your God, and rise up and build a sanctuary for your God, to bring in the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the holy vessels of God into the house being built for the name of the Lord."
verses.23:1: And David was an old man and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king in his place over Israel.
verses.23:2: And he gathered all the chiefs of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.
verses.23:3: And the Levites counted from thirty years old and upward, and their number, head by head, came to thirty-eight thousand men:
verses.23:4: of the overseers over the works of the house, twenty-four thousand, and scribes and judges, six thousand,
verses.23:5: and four thousand praising the Lord with the instruments which he made to praise the Lord.
verses.23:6: And David divided them into courses for the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, Merari.
verses.23:7: And for Parosom: for Edan and for Shimei.
verses.23:8: The sons of Edan: the chief Jehiel, and Zetham, and Joel. And three
verses.23:9: sons of Shimei: Alothim, and Hieiel, and Haidan, three; these were chiefs of the paternal families of Edan.
verses.23:10: And for the sons of Shimei: Jahath, and Ziza, and Joash, and Beriah; these were the sons of Shimei, four.
verses.23:11: And Jahath was the chief, and Ziza the second; and Joash and Beriah did not multiply sons, and they became a paternal house, for one enrollment.
verses.23:12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel, four.
verses.23:13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to be consecrated as most holy, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to serve and to invoke a blessing in His name forever.
verses.23:14: And as for Moses, the man of God, his sons were called into the tribe of Levi.
verses.23:15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.23:16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
verses.23:17: And the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the chief, and there were no other sons; and the sons of Rehabiah increased to a high degree.
verses.23:18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomoth the chief.
verses.23:19: Of the sons of Hebron: Idud the chief, Amadiah the second, Uzziel the third, Ikemias the fourth.
verses.23:20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
verses.23:21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
verses.23:22: And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their brothers, took them.
verses.23:23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, and Aidath, and Arimoth, three.
verses.23:24: These were the sons of Levi according to their paternal houses, chiefs of their paternal families according to their enrollment, according to the number of their names, head by head, doing the works of the service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:25: For David said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and has settled in Jerusalem forever."
verses.23:26: And the Levites were not carrying the tent and all its vessels for its service;
verses.23:27: for in the last words of David is the number of the sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward,
verses.23:28: for he stationed them at the hand of Aaron to serve in the house of the Lord, over the courts and over the chambers, and over the cleansing of all the holy things, and over the works of the service of God;
verses.23:29: for the loaves of the presentation, for the fine flour of the offering, and for the unleavened wafers, and for a griddle, and for that which is mixed, and for every measure;
verses.23:30: and to stand in the morning to praise, to give thanks to the Lord, and likewise in the evening;
verses.23:31: and over all the burnt offerings offered up to the Lord on the Sabbaths, and on the new moons, and at the feasts, according to number, according to the ordinance upon them, continually to the Lord.
verses.23:32: And they shall keep the charges of the tent of testimony and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brothers, to serve in the house of the Lord.
verses.24:1: And as for the sons of Aaron by division: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.24:2: And Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; and Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, served as priests.
verses.24:3: And David divided them, and Zadok of the sons of Eleazar, and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their enrollment, according to their service, according to their paternal houses.
verses.24:4: And the sons of Eleazar were found more numerous in chiefs of the mighty men than the sons of Ithamar; and he divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, chiefs for paternal houses, sixteen; for the sons of Aaron, Ithamar, according to paternal houses.
verses.24:5: And he divided them by lots, these with those, for there were chiefs of the holy things and chiefs of the Lord among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.
verses.24:6: And Shemaiah the son of Nethanel, the scribe, of Levi, wrote them down in the presence of the king and the chiefs, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the chiefs of the paternal families of the priests and of the Levites: of a paternal house, one by one for Eleazar and one by one for Ithamar.
verses.24:7: And the first lot came out for Jarim, for Anaidiah the second,
verses.24:8: for Hareb the third, for Seorim the fourth,
verses.24:9: for Malchijah the fifth, for Benjamin the sixth,
verses.24:10: for Koz the seventh, for Abijah the eighth,
verses.24:11: for Jeshua the ninth, for Ischaniah the tenth,
verses.24:12: for Eliabiei the eleventh, for Jakim the twelfth,
verses.24:13: for Hocchoppha the thirteenth, for Gelba the fourteenth,
verses.24:14: for Immer the fifteenth, for Hezin the sixteenth,
verses.24:15: for Aphese the seventeenth, for Pethahiah the eighteenth,
verses.24:16: for Ezekiel the nineteenth, for Achim the twentieth,
verses.24:17: for Gamul the twenty-first, for Adallai the twenty-second,
verses.24:19: This was their enrollment according to their service, to enter into the house of the Lord according to their ordinance by the hand of Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel commanded.
verses.24:20: And for the remaining sons of Levi: for the sons of Amram, Jobael, Jehdeiah;
verses.24:22: And for the Izharite, Shelomoth; for the sons of Shelomoth, Inath.
verses.24:23: The sons of Jedimu: Amadiah the second, Jase the third, Jokom the fourth.
verses.24:24: Of Uzziel, Micah; the sons of Micah, Shamir;
verses.24:25: the brother of Micah, Isshiah; the son of Isshiah, Zechariah.
verses.24:26: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Uzziah:
verses.24:27: of Merari, for Uzziah, his sons: Isoam, and Zaccur, and Abai.
verses.24:28: For Mahli: Eleazar and Ithamar; and Eleazar died, and he had no sons.
verses.24:29: For Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
verses.24:30: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, and Elah, and Arimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their paternal houses.
verses.24:31: And they also received lots just as their brothers the sons of Aaron, before the king, and Zadok, and Ahimelech, and the chief of the paternal families of the priests and of the Levites, the patriarchs of Araab, just as his younger brothers.
verses.25:1: And King David and the leaders of the army appointed for the tasks the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who spoke out with lyres, with harps, and with cymbals; and their count, as they worked at their tasks, was head by head.
verses.25:2: The sons of Asaph: Sacchus, Joseph, Nathalias, and Erael; the sons of Asaph, next to the king.
verses.25:3: For Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Tuna, Zeri, Saia, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, following their father Jeduthun, who sounded forth thanksgiving and praise to the Lord with a lyre.
verses.25:4: For Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Azarel, Shubael, Amsu, Jeremoth, Hananiah, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romei; the sons of Od, and Jeibasaka, Manthei, Hothir, and Melzoth.
verses.25:5: All these were sons of Heman, who sounded forth for the king in the words of God to exalt a horn; and God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
verses.25:6: All these were with their father, singing hymns in the house of God with cymbals, with harps, and with lyres, next to the king, and Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
verses.25:7: And their number along with their brothers, taught to sing to the Lord—everyone with understanding—was two hundred and eighty-eight.
verses.25:8: And they also cast lots for turns of duty, small and great alike, both the fully trained and the learners.
verses.25:9: And the first lot of his sons and his brothers came out for Asaph, for Joseph; Galuia the second, Heneia, his brothers and his sons, twelve;
verses.25:10: the third, Zacchuth, his son, and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:11: the fourth, Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:12: the fifth, Nathan, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:13: the sixth, Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:14: the seventh, Jeseriel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:15: the eighth, Josiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:16: the ninth, Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:17: the tenth, Emei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:18: the eleventh, Azariah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:19: the twelfth, Haria, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:20: the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:21: the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:22: the fifteenth, Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:23: the sixteenth, Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:24: the seventeenth, Bakata, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:25: the eighteenth, Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:26: the nineteenth, Methathei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:27: the twentieth, Aematha, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:28: the twenty-first, Hethei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:29: the twenty-second, Godomathei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:30: the twenty-third, Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.25:31: the twenty-fourth, Romelchei, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.26:1: For the divisions of the gates, the sons of the Korahites: Mosolael the son of Kore; from the sons of Abijah, Saphar.
verses.26:2: And as for Mosalea, son of Zechariah: the firstborn Iderel, Zechariah, Jenonel,
verses.26:4: And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jozabad, Joath, Sacar, Naas, Jehiel,
verses.26:5: Ammiel, Issachar, Japhthoslaathi; for God blessed him.
verses.26:6: And to his son Shemaiah were born sons of the firstborn Rosai for his father's house, for they were mighty.
verses.26:7: The sons of Shemaiah: Goonei, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, and Ahihud—mighty sons—Ennu, Sabchia, and Isbakom.
verses.26:8: All from the sons of Obed-edom, they and their brothers and their sons, acting mightily in the work, were sixty-two in all for Obed-edom.
verses.26:9: And Mosomameid had sons and brothers, eighteen mighty men.
verses.26:10: And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons keeping the leadership, for he was not the firstborn; and his father made him leader of the second division.
verses.26:11: Tablai the third, Zechariah; all these sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
verses.26:12: To these—to the leaders of the mighty men—belonged the divisions of the gates, with turns of duty just like their brothers, to serve in the house of the Lord.
verses.26:13: And they cast lots, small and great alike, according to the houses of their ancestral families, for gateway after gateway.
verses.26:14: And the lot for those toward the east fell to Shelemiah and Zechariah, sons of Soaz; for Malchiah they cast lots, and the lot came out for the north;
verses.26:15: for Obed-edom, the south, opposite the house of Esephin;
verses.26:16: secondly, for Hosah toward the west, past the gate of the chamber of the ascent; watch opposite watch.
verses.26:17: Toward the east, six a day; on the north, four a day; on the south, four a day; and for the Esephin, two
verses.26:18: as reliefs, and for Hosah toward the west, past the gate of the chamber, three. Watch opposite watch of the ascent: toward the east, six a day, and on the north, four, and on the south, four, and for Esephim, two as reliefs, and toward the west, four, and for the path, two relieving one another.
verses.26:19: These are the divisions of the gatekeepers for the sons of Kohath and for the Merarites.
verses.26:20: And the Levites, their brothers, were over the treasuries of the house of the Lord and over the treasuries of the consecrated things.
verses.26:21: These were the sons of Chadan, the Gershonite: for Ladan, and Jaieel son of Jehu; the sons of Jehiel, leaders of ancestral families for Ladan; for the Gershonite, Jehiel.
verses.26:22: The sons of Jehiel, Zetham and Joel, the brothers, were over the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
verses.26:23: For Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
verses.26:24: And Joel, son of Gershom, son of Moses, was over the treasuries.
verses.26:25: And his brother Eliezer had a son Rehabiah, and Hoshaiah, and Joram, and Zichri, and Shelomoth.
verses.26:26: Shelomoth himself and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the holy things that King David, and the leaders of the ancestral families, the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, and the commanders of the army consecrated,
verses.26:27: which he took from cities and from the spoils, and consecrated from them so that the building of the house of God would not fall short;
verses.26:28: and over all the holy things of God, of Samuel the prophet, and of Saul son of Kish, and of Abner son of Ner, and of Joab son of Zeruiah—everything that he consecrated was by the hand of Shelomoth and his brothers.
verses.26:29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and sons of the outside work were over Israel, to act as scribes and to judge.
verses.26:30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, the mighty men, one thousand seven hundred, were over the supervision of Israel beyond the Jordan toward the west, for all the service of the Lord and the work of the king.
verses.26:31: Of the Hebronites, Tudeias was the leader of the Hebronites, according to their generations, by ancestral families. In the fortieth year of his reign they were inspected, and a mighty man was found among them in Riazer of Gilead.
verses.26:32: And his brothers, the mighty sons, were two thousand seven hundred, the leaders of ancestral families; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every ordinance of the Lord and matter of the king.
verses.27:1: Now the sons of Israel according to their number, leaders of the fathers' houses, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and scribes who served the people and in every matter of the king according to divisions, every matter of the one coming in and going out month by month, for all the months of the year: one division was twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:2: And over the first division of the first month was Sobal the son of Zabdiel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:3: He was from the sons of Perez, leader of all the leaders of the army of the first month.
verses.27:4: And over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ekchoch, and in his division were twenty-four thousand, leaders of the army.
verses.27:5: The third, for the third month, was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the priest, the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:6: This Benaiah was mightier than the thirty and over the thirty; and over his division was Laibazath his son.
verses.27:7: The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Obadiah his son, and the brothers; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:8: The fifth, for the fifth month, was the ruler Salaoth the Ezrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:9: The sixth, for the sixth month, was Hodaviah the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:10: The seventh, for the seventh month, was Chesles from Phallous, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:11: The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of Zerah; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:12: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer from Anathoth, from the land of Benjamin; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:13: The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai from Netophah, of Zerah; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:14: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah from Pirathon, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:15: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai from Netophah, of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:16: And over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the ruler was Eliezer the son of Zichri; for Simeon, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.27:17: for Levi, Hashabiah the son of Samuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
verses.27:18: for Judah, Eliab, of the brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri the son of Mishael;
verses.27:19: for Zebulun, Shemaiah the son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
verses.27:20: for Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Uzziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Phaladaia;
verses.27:21: for the half-tribe of Manasseh, those in Gilead, Jaddai the son of Zabdiah; for the sons of Benjamin, Asier the son of Abner;
verses.27:22: for Dan, Azarel the son of Joram. These were the patriarchs of the tribes of Israel.
verses.27:23: And David did not take their number from twenty years old and under, because the Lord had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
verses.27:24: And Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number among the people, and did not finish; and because of these things wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not recorded in the book of the chronicles of King David.
verses.27:25: And over the storehouses of the king was Azmaveth the son of Adiel, and over the storehouses in the field, and in the villages, and in the hamlets, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah.
verses.27:26: And over those farming the land, the workers, was Ezri the son of Chobud.
verses.27:27: And over the estates was Shimei from Rael, and over the storehouses of wine in the estates was Zichri the son of Sephni.

verses.27:32: And Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding; and Jehiel the son of Hachami was with the king's sons.

verses.28:1: And David assembled all the leaders of Israel, leaders of the judges, and the leaders of the divisions around the king's person, and leaders of the thousands and of the hundreds, and the treasurers, and those over his property, and the mighty men, and the warriors, in Jerusalem.
verses.28:2: And David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, "Listen to me, brothers and my people. It came upon my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord and a standing place for the feet of our Lord, and I prepared the things needed for the dwelling place.
verses.28:3: But God said, 'You shall not build a house for Me to call My name upon it, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'
verses.28:4: And the Lord, the God of Israel, chose me from all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever; and in Judah He has chosen the kingdom, and from the house of Judah, the house of my father; in me He took pleasure, that I should become king over all Israel.
verses.28:5: And from all my sons, because the Lord gave me many sons, He chose Solomon my son to seat him on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
verses.28:6: And God said to me, 'Solomon your son will inherit My house and My court, because I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be a father to him.
verses.28:7: And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is strong to keep My commandments and My judgments as on this day.'
verses.28:8: And now, in the sight of all the assembly of the Lord, seek the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may inherit the good land for our sons forever.
verses.28:9: And now, Solomon, know the God of your fathers and serve with a complete heart and a willing soul, because the Lord examines all hearts and knows every thought; if you seek Him, He will be found by you, and if you forsake Him, He will forsake you to the end.
verses.28:10: See, therefore: the Lord has chosen you to build a house for Him as a sanctuary; be strong and act."
verses.28:11: Then David gave Solomon his son the pattern of the temple, and of its houses, and of its zakcho, and of the upper rooms, and of the inner storerooms, and of the house of atonement,
verses.28:12: and the pattern that he had in his spirit of the courts of the house of the Lord, and of all the chambers all around, those for the storerooms of the Lord and of the storerooms of the holy things,
verses.28:13: and of the lodging rooms of the divisions of the priests and of the Levites for all the work of the service of the house of the Lord, and of the storerooms of the vessels of service.
verses.28:14: And he gave him the measure of their weight, both of the gold and of the silver, the weight of the lampstands
verses.28:16: Likewise he gave him the weight of the tables of the presentation, of each gold table, and in the same way of the silver ones,
verses.28:17: and of the meat hooks and libation vessels and the gold bowls, and the weight of the gold and of the silver ones, for each weight.
verses.28:18: And he showed him the weight of the altar of incense of refined gold, and the pattern of the chariot of the cherubim with their wings spread out and overshadowing the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.28:19: David gave to Solomon all things in writing from the hand of the Lord, according to the understanding that had come to him of the workmanship of the pattern.
verses.28:20: And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous and act; do not fear and do not be terrified, because the Lord my God is with you; He will not fail you and will by no means forsake you until you finish all the work of the service of the house of the Lord. The pattern of the temple and of its house and of its sakcho, and the upper rooms, and the inner storerooms, and the house of atonement, and the pattern of the house of the Lord.
verses.28:21: And here are the divisions of the priests and of the Levites for all the service of the house of the Lord, and with you in every undertaking, and every willing person with wisdom in every craft, and the leaders and all the people for all your commands."
verses.29:1: And King David said to all the assembly, "Solomon my son, whom the Lord has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great, for it is not for man, but for the Lord God.
verses.29:2: According to all my ability, I have prepared for the house of my God gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, soom stones and stones for setting, and costly and multicolored stones, and every precious stone, and much Parian marble.
verses.29:3: And moreover, because I take delight in the house of my God, I have gold and silver that I have acquired for myself, and look, I have given it for the house of my God above measure, apart from what I have prepared for the house of the holy things:
verses.29:4: three thousand talents of the gold from Suphir and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for the walls of the temple to be overlaid with them
verses.29:5: by the hand of craftsmen. And who is willing to fill his hands today for the Lord?"
verses.29:6: And leaders of ancestral houses, and the leaders of the sons of Israel, and the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the overseers of the works, and the builders of the king offered willingly.
verses.29:7: And they gave for the works of the house of the Lord five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand gold coins, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
verses.29:8: And those with whom a stone was found gave it to the storehouses of the house of the Lord by the hand of Besiel the Gersomnite.
verses.29:9: And the people rejoiced over offering willingly, because with a full heart they offered willingly to the Lord, and King David rejoiced greatly.
verses.29:10: And King David blessed the Lord in the presence of the assembly, saying,
verses.29:11: "Blessed are You, Lord, the God of Israel, our Father from eternity and to eternity. You, Lord, are the greatness and the power and the boast and the victory and the strength, for You hold dominion over all things in heaven and on the earth; before Your face every king and nation is shaken.
verses.29:12: From You come wealth and glory; You rule over all things, Lord, the Ruler of every rule; and in Your hand are strength and might, and it is in Your hand, Almighty, to make great and to strengthen all things.
verses.29:13: And now, Lord, we give thanks to You and praise the name of Your boasting.
verses.29:14: And who am I, and who are Your people, that we have had the strength to offer willingly to You in this way? For all things are Yours, and from what is Yours we have given to You.
verses.29:15: For we are sojourners before You and residents, like all our fathers. Like a shadow are our days on earth, and there is no endurance.
verses.29:16: Lord our God, as for all this abundance that I have prepared for a house to be built for Your holy name, it is from Your hand, and all things belong to You.
verses.29:17: And I know, Lord, that You are the One who examines hearts, and You love righteousness. In sincerity of heart I have willingly offered all these things, and now I have seen Your people who are found here offering willingly to You with gladness.
verses.29:18: Lord, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel our fathers, guard these things in the thought of the heart of Your people forever, and direct their hearts toward You.
verses.29:19: And to Solomon my son give a good heart to do Your commandments and Your testimonies and Your statutes, and to bring to completion the construction of Your house."
verses.29:20: And David said to all the assembly, "Bless the Lord our God." And all the assembly blessed the Lord, the God of their fathers, and bending their knees, they bowed down to the Lord and to the king.
verses.29:21: And David sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings to God on the day after the first day: one thousand calves, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, and their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
verses.29:22: And they ate and drank before the Lord on that day with joy, and they made Solomon the son of David king, and anointed him to the Lord as king and Zadok to the priesthood.
verses.29:23: And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and he was favored, and all Israel obeyed him.
verses.29:24: The leaders and the mighty men and the sons of King David his father submitted to him.
verses.29:25: And the Lord made Solomon great from above, before all Israel; and they gave him the glory of a king, such as had not been upon any king before him.
verses.29:26: And David the son of Jesse reigned over Israel
verses.29:27: forty years: in Hebron seven years, in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
verses.29:28: And he died in a good old age, full of days, in wealth and glory; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:29: Now the rest of the deeds of King David, the former and the latter, are written in the accounts of Samuel the seer and in the accounts of Nathan the prophet and in the accounts of Gad the seer,
verses.29:30: concerning all his kingdom and his might, which came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the earth. Solomon the son of David grew strong over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and made him grow to the heights.

notes.1:10: Greek reads "giant hunter" (aligning with Gen 10:9 LXX) rather than MT "mighty one." In vv. 5-9 the Greek also adds Elishah among the sons of Japheth (v. 5), reads Riphath (v. 6) and "the Rhodians" (v. 7) where MT has Diphath and Rodanim, and reads Judadan (v. 9, absorbing the Hebrew conjunction) for MT Dedan.
notes.1:17: The Old Greek text omits vv. 11-16 and vv. 18-23, passing directly from Shem's sons Elam and Asshur to Arpachshad and the patriarchal line down to Abraham (vv. 24-27, where v. 27 reads simply "Abraham" without MT "Abram, that is").
notes.1:30: Verses 29-37 preserve several LXX-distinct readings and names: "of the firstborn of Ishmael" with Nabdael, Massa, Mama, Iduma, Manasseh, Chondan, and Teman (vv. 29-30); reversed pairs Midian/Medan and Dedan/Sheba alongside Sobak and Gapher (vv. 32-33); "Jacob and Esau" (v. 34, MT "Esau and Israel"); and Jeul, Zophar, "by Timna, Amalek" (clarifying Timna as mother), and Omoze (vv. 35-37).
notes.1:40: The Horite genealogy in vv. 38-42 differs extensively in the Greek: Onan appears in place of Ezer and Dishan (v. 38), Onam (v. 40), and Jaakan (v. 42); Heman, Elath, and Namna appear in v. 39 instead of Homam and Lotan's sister Timna; and vv. 40-42 read Solam, Machanam, Sob, Aith, Sonan (for Anah), Gethram, Balaam (for Bilhan), and Zukam (for Zaavan).
notes.1:47: Verses 43-54 preserve a major LXX textual dislocation: v. 43 omits the reference to Edom and Israel's kings, v. 47 breaks off before its subject, v. 48 repeats Hadad's death, and v. 49 contains the displaced king Balaennor son of Achbor (MT Baal-hanan). Distinct Greek names in this section also include Balak (vv. 43-44), Barad and Gittaim (v. 46), Samaa from Masekkah (v. 48), Hadad son of Barad and Peor without his wife's name (v. 50), and Teman, Gola, Jetheth, Elibamas, Mazar, Mediel, and Zaphoin (vv. 51-54, MT Timna, Alvah, Jetheth ... Iram).
notes.2:9: The Greek lists four sons of Hezron (Jerahmeel, Ram, Chabel, and Aram) and names Arran in v. 10, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists three sons (Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai) with Ram in v. 10. Throughout vv. 3-17, the Septuagint also preserves several distinct proper-name forms, including Aua (v. 3), Harson and Jemuel (v. 5), Calca (v. 6), Zaria (v. 8), Zaddai (v. 14), and Amasab (v. 17).
notes.2:18: The Greek takes Azubah and Elioth as direct objects of "fathered" ("Azubah, a wife, and Elioth") rather than "with Azubah his wife and with Jerioth" as in the Hebrew, and names her sons Joasar, Jasub, and Orna (Hebrew: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon).
notes.2:24: The Greek reads "Caleb came to Ephrathah" (with Ascho as Abijah's son), whereas the Hebrew reads "in Caleb-ephrathah" (with Ashhur). Similarly, vv. 21-23 preserve the distinct Greek names Serug, Arran, and Sair (Hebrew: Segub, Aram, and Jair).
notes.2:32: The Greek reads the Hebrew "Jada, brother of Shammai" as a father and an additional first son ("Iduda: Achisamas"), yielding three sons instead of two. Surrounding verses (vv. 25-49) likewise preserve numerous Septuagint-distinct names, such as Ozom, Alsalad, Ephraim, Isemiel, Jochel, Joshua (vv. 38, 47), Emas, Jaklan, Gedsur, Gaiphael, Peleg, and Sagae.
notes.2:51: The Greek expands the line into three pairs (Solomon of Betha, Lammon of Bethlehem, and Harim of Beth-gaidon; Hebrew: Salma of Bethlehem and Hareph of Beth-gader). Verses 52-55 also follow distinct Septuagint readings, including transliterated clan names, "the cities of Jair" (v. 53), Solomon again (v. 54), and "the families of writings" (v. 55, reflecting Hebrew sepharim "writings" rather than sopherim "scribes").
notes.3:1: The Greek reads "Israelite" (rather than Hebrew "Jezreelitess") and "Damniel" (rather than Hebrew "Daniel"); similarly, vv. 2-8 preserve several distinct Septuagint name forms (such as Thoamai, Sabital, Ala, Baar, Elisha, Naphath, and Janue, plus Bathsheba in v. 5 for Hebrew Bath-shua).
notes.3:4: The Greek omits the clause found in the Hebrew stating that David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron.
notes.3:11: The Greek reads "Ozia" where the Hebrew has "Ahaziah," and in v. 14 reads "Amnon" where the Hebrew has "Amon."
notes.3:19: The Greek makes Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel (rather than Hebrew Pedaiah) and omits Shimei and the heading "the sons of Zerubbabel."
notes.3:21: Unlike the Hebrew, which lists parallel clans ("sons of..."), the Greek repeats "his son," extending Hananiah's lineage linearly; vv. 18-24 also preserve several Septuagint-distinct personal names (including Phaldaias, Denethi, Osa, Arobasok, Joel, Marei, Noadiah, Elithana/Elithenan, and Asib).
notes.4:5: Verses 1-20 contain numerous Septuagint-distinct personal and place names diverging from the Hebrew (including Harson in v. 1, Bethladen in v. 4, Sara, Aoda, Thoada, and Loada in vv. 5-7, "brother of Rechab" in v. 8, Gelia and Noroel in v. 18, and the expanded list in v. 19).
notes.4:9: The Greek renders Hebrew "Jabez" as "Igabes" and leaves the etymological wordplay untranslated as "as gabes" (where the Hebrew reads "in pain").
notes.4:10: The Greek reads "make knowledge so as not to humble me," diverging markedly from the Hebrew ("keep from harm so that it may not pain me"), and adds "all" before "that he asked."
notes.4:21: The Greek leaves the Hebrew expression for linen-working untranslated as "ephrath habak," and in v. 22 leaves the final clause untranslated as "habederein athoukiein" (Hebrew: "the records are ancient").
notes.4:22: Greek leaves the Hebrew phrase for "and the records are ancient" untranslated as the transliterated words habederein athoukiein.
notes.4:26: The Greek omits Hammuel and Zaccur before Shimei; in v. 27 it reads "three daughters" (Hebrew: "six") and "their brothers," and in v. 32 lists four towns while keeping the total "five cities."
notes.4:39: The Greek reads "Gerar" (Hebrew: "Gedor") and treats Hebrew "the valley" as the proper name "Gai"; in v. 41 it reads "their houses" (Hebrew: "their tents") and "Minaeans," and in v. 43 omits "and they lived there."
notes.5:1: Greek reads 'his blessing' here and in v. 2 (MT 'birthright') and singular 'his son Joseph' (MT 'the sons of Joseph').
notes.5:4: The Greek Reubenite genealogy (vv. 4-8) diverges from MT, reading 'Shimei' and the proper name 'Benaiah' (for MT 'his son') here, 'Echa,' 'Recha,' 'Joel,' and 'Beel' in vv. 5-6, 'Joel' in v. 7, and 'Balek' and 'Beelmasson' in v. 8.
notes.5:13: Greek lists seven names, including 'Chima' (MT Jacan) and 'Obed' (MT Eber), yet totals them as 'eight' (MT 'seven'). Elsewhere in vv. 10-16, Greek reads 'resident aliens' (v. 10, MT Hagrites), 'Elcha,' 'Sabat,' 'Janin the scribe' (vv. 11-12), 'Abihaia,' 'Idai,' 'Isai,' 'Juri,' 'Zabucham' (v. 14), and 'Geriam' (v. 16).
notes.5:21: Greek reads 'five thousand camels' (MT fifty thousand), with other notable LXX readings in vv. 19-24 including 'Turaeans' and 'Naphisadaeans' (v. 19), 'prevailed over them' and 'encampments' (v. 20), and 'Baileim,' 'in Lebanon,' 'Sei,' and 'Jeliel' (vv. 23-24).
notes.5:26: Greek reads 'Phaloch' (MT Pul), 'Chaach' (MT Halah), and 'Chozar' (MT Gozan) while omitting MT's Hara; Tiglath-pileser appears in Greek as Thalgabanasar (v. 6) and Thagnaphamasar (v. 26).
notes.5:32: Greek reads 'Mariel' here and in v. 33 (MT Meraioth). Verses 27-41 follow the LXX and Hebrew chapter division (1 Chronicles 6:1-15 in most English Bibles), with v. 41 omitting MT's mention of the Lord.
notes.6:6: In the Gershonite and Kohathite lines (vv. 6-13), the Greek preserves several distinct names compared to the Masoretic Text (MT 6:21-28): Joab, Adi, and Jaara (v. 6; MT Joah, Iddo, Zerah); Haresi (v. 7; MT Assir); Zophai and Kainath (v. 8; MT Ebiasaph, Assir); Kohath (v. 9; MT Tahath); Alimoth (v. 10; MT Ahimoth); Abiathar and Aseri (v. 11; MT Zophai, Nahath); Idaer (v. 12; MT Jeroham); and Sani (v. 13; MT Vashni).
notes.6:14: The Greek text omits 'Merari: Mahli' at the start of the verse (cf. MT 6:29), leaving 'Sons:' followed immediately by 'Libni his son.'
notes.6:16: Literally 'over the hands of the singers,' rendering a Hebrew idiom for overseeing musical service. In v. 17 the Greek also preserves distinct readings: 'the tabernacle of the house of testimony' (MT 'tabernacle of the tent of meeting') and 'with instruments' (MT 'with singing').
notes.6:19: In the genealogies of Heman and Asaph (vv. 19-28), the adopted Greek critical text (Codex Vaticanus/Swete) reads Eaal and Theie in v. 19 (Sixtine/Brenton: Jeroboam and Tohu; MT: Jeroham and Toah), Amathiu (v. 20; MT Amasai), Abiasar (v. 22; MT Ebiasaph), Maasai (v. 25; MT Baaseiah), Aziah (v. 26; MT Adaiah), and Echa (v. 28; MT Jahath).
notes.6:31: The Greek omits Hilkiah and Amzi between Amaziah and Bani (cf. MT 6:46).
notes.6:32: The adopted Greek critical text (following Codex Vaticanus/Swete) reads 'υἱοῦ Μοολεὶ Μοσεὶ' without repeating 'υἱοῦ' ('son of') before Mushi; other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew text supply 'son of' before Mushi.
notes.6:36: In the priestly line (vv. 36-38), the adopted Greek critical text (Codex Vaticanus/Swete) reads Bokai (v. 36; conventional Bukki) and Zerahiah (Zaraia, v. 36; Sixtine/Brenton reads Seraiah), Mariel (v. 37; MT Meraioth) and Aliareia (v. 37; Sixtine/Brenton and MT: Amariah), and Ahisama (v. 38; MT Ahimaaz).
notes.6:42: Among the Aaronite cities (vv. 42-45), the Greek preserves distinct names and an extra city compared to the Masoretic Text (MT 6:57-60): Selna (v. 42; MT Jattir), Jeththar and Debir (v. 43; MT Hilen and Debir), Attan (v. 44; absent in MT, cf. Josh 21:16 Juttah), and Anchoch (v. 45; MT Anathoth).
notes.6:48: The Greek reads 'the tribe of Dan' where the Masoretic Text has 'the tribe of Gad' (MT 6:63; cf. v. 65). Similarly, v. 50 omits 'the tribe of the sons of Benjamin' (cf. MT 6:65).
notes.6:54: In the Kohathite and Gershonite city lists (vv. 53-61), the Greek omits Bileam (v. 55) and differs from the Masoretic Text (MT 6:68-76) in several names: Ikaam (v. 53; MT Jokmeam), Eglam and Gethoron (v. 54; MT Aijalon and Gath-rimmon), Amar (v. 55; MT Aner), Aseroth (v. 56; MT Ashtaroth), Deberi and Dabor (v. 57; MT Daberath), Enan (v. 58; MT Anem), Maasa and Abaran (v. 59; MT Mashal and Abdon), and Hammoth (v. 61; MT Hammon).
notes.6:63: The Greek reads 'and Jericho toward the west of the Jordan' (MT 6:78 'at Jericho, east of the Jordan') and omits Jahzah. In the Merarite list (vv. 62-66), the Greek also reads Thachchia (v. 62; MT Tabor), Kadamos and Maephla (v. 64; MT Kedemoth and Mephaath), Rammon-gilead and Maanaith (v. 65; MT Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim), and Gezer (v. 66; MT Jazer).
notes.7:3: The Greek text lists Michael under Zirri rather than Zaria and preserves distinctive forms for several genealogical names in vv. 1-3 (including Tholaek, Thole, and Tholai for Tola, as well as Phut, Jassur, Raphara, Riel, Eikan, Basan, Isamuel, Zirri, Zaria, Mibdia, and Rael) where it diverges from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:6: The Greek reads "Benjamin, Abira, and Adiel, three," omitting Bela here and preserving LXX-distinct names across the Benjaminite, Naphtalite, and Manassite lists in vv. 6-19 (such as Badee, Abachi/Amachir, Ariel, Ramessai, Sapphin, Happhin, Raom, Solomon, Balam, Hamphin, Mamphin, Sapphaad, Suros, Badam, and Semira).
notes.7:21: The Greek has singular "him" (αὐτόν) rather than plural "them," preserves a shorter Ephraimite lineage in vv. 20-21 (Sothalath, Laada, Noome, Ozar), and reads plural "their brothers" (ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν) in v. 22.
notes.7:24: The Greek attaches "and among those who remained" (καὶ ἐν ἐκείνοις τοῖς καταλοίποις) to Ephraim's naming of Bargaa from v. 23 instead of naming a daughter Sheerah, making "he" the subject of "built" and rendering the Hebrew place name Uzzen-sheerah as a personal lineage ("the sons of Ozan: Seera and Raphe").
notes.7:26: Following Codex Vaticanus/Swete, the Greek critical text reads plural 'sons of Amioueid, sons of Eleimasai' (υἱοὶ Ἀμιουείδ, υἱοὶ Ἐλειμασαί), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew read singular 'Ammihud his son, Elishama his son.'
notes.7:29: The Greek includes an extra town (Balad) alongside LXX-distinct place names (Naarnan, Gaian, Thalme) in vv. 28-29 and ends with singular "in this" (ἐν ταύτῃ) rather than plural "in these"; vv. 25-27 and 30-39 likewise preserve numerous LXX-distinct personal names (including Gedson, Jeeth, Zemma, Num, Beriga/Bericha, Gaber, Iphamel/Aphalech/Japhalel, Hobab, Balaam, and Sophas).
notes.8:1: The Greek text preserves numerous distinct proper names throughout this genealogy that differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text—here reading Beleleel (though Bela in 8:3), Saba, Japhael, and (in 8:2) Joa instead of Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, and Nohah. Similar Greek-distinct name forms appear throughout verses 3-27 and 29-40 (for example, Ali, Abisamas, Saarel, Hada, Alphaad, Obed, Semer, Elchaad, Samaith, Molcha, Abalon, Baalakaim, Zak, Salasath, and Asel).
notes.8:7: Greek reads the proper name Higaam (Ἱγαάμ), reflecting a transliteration of the Hebrew verb meaning 'he deported them', and names his sons Naana and Jachichol where Hebrew has Uzza and Ahihud.
notes.8:12: Greek reads Onan (Ὠνάν) and omits Lod where Hebrew has Ono and Lod; in verse 13 Greek likewise reads Elam (Αἰλάμ) where Hebrew has Aijalon, and in verses 14 and 31 renders Hebrew Ahio as 'his brother'.
notes.8:33: Greek reads Amminadab (Ἀμειναδάβ) where Hebrew has Abinadab, and in verse 34 uses the plural 'sons' before Merib-baal; in verse 36 Greek gives Zak (Hebrew: Ahaz) two sons, Jad and Jada, corresponding to Hebrew Jehoaddah.
notes.8:38: Greek states that Azel had six sons but lists only five names because it translates the Hebrew second name Bocheru as 'his firstborn' (πρωτότοκος αὐτοῦ) after Ezrikai (Hebrew: Azrikam).
notes.9:2: The Greek reads 'in the cities of Israel' followed by 'Levite sons, the priests, and those who were given' (Greek 'hoi dedomenoi,' literally rendering the Hebrew Nethinim, or temple servants). In 9:1 the Greek likewise joins 'Judah' to 'the kings of Israel and Judah' rather than starting a separate clause about Judah's exile.
notes.9:8: The Greek reads 'and these were the sons of Uzzi son of Machir' (interpreting Hebrew Elah as 'these' and Michri as Machir), alongside other distinct Septuagint names across 9:4-17 such as Gothi, Sammiu, Epiel, Shallum, Moollam, Haana, Banaam, Benaiah, Joiarim, Marmoth, Jediu, Bakar, Rarael, Gilead, Jothon, Ossa, Akum, Tammam, and Aimam.
notes.9:20: The Greek reads 'and these were with him' instead of 'and the Lord was with him.' In 9:19 it likewise preserves the distinct Septuagint readings 'Solomon son of Koreb' (for Shallum son of Kore) and 'guarding the watches' (for thresholds).
notes.9:32: The Greek treats Hebrew 'sons of' as the proper name 'Benaiah the Kohathite.' Similarly, 9:31 adds 'of the high priest' to the griddle sacrifice, and 9:33 reads 'appointed divisions' where the Hebrew describes chambers free from other service.
notes.9:44: Although six sons are stated, only five names appear because the Greek renders Hebrew Bocheru as 'his firstborn.' Elsewhere in 9:36-43 the Greek preserves distinct readings including Sabadon, Isir, Jedur, 'a brother' (translating Ahio as a common noun in 9:37), Jada, Gameleth, Gazaoth, Baana, and the omission of Eleasah before Azel (Greek 'Esael').
notes.10:1: Greek 'allophyloi' (literally 'foreigners') is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines from Judges onward and is translated consistently throughout this chapter.
notes.10:3: Unlike the singular Hebrew text, the Greek uses plural forms ('found them ... they suffered pain'), includes 'and pains,' and reads 'from the bows' rather than 'from the archers.'
notes.10:10: The Greek reads plural 'their armor' (rather than 'his armor'), singular 'their god,' and 'placed his head' rather than 'fastened his skull.'
notes.10:13: The clause 'and Samuel the prophet answered him' is a notable Septuagint addition not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (cf. 1 Samuel 28:15-19).
notes.11:2: The Greek text reads "eipen Israel Kyrios soi" (lit. "Israel's Lord / the Lord of Israel said to you"), a distinctive Septuagint reading where other witnesses have "the Lord your God said to you."
notes.11:8: The Septuagint has the shorter, distinctive clause "and he fought and took the city" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions the Millo and Joab restoring the rest of the city.
notes.11:13: Greek "allophyloi" (lit. "foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard term for the Philistines in Samuel and Chronicles, and "Phasodome" preserves the distinctive Greek form of the place name (cf. MT Pas-dammim).
notes.11:22: Greek translates the preposition comparatively as "beyond Kabzeel" (rather than "from Kabzeel") and leaves Hebrew "ariel" untranslated ("the two ariels of Moab"), a rare term often understood as "lion-like heroes" or "champions."
notes.11:25: The Greek text reads "over his family" ("patrian") where the Hebrew has "over his bodyguard," and in 11:24 uses the shortened patronymic "Joad" for Jehoiada.
notes.11:34: Throughout the warrior list (11:11-47), the Septuagint preserves numerous Greek-distinct personal, place, and gentilic names (such as Jesebada, the Archonite, Nachali Gaash, and Bennaias the Somologennounin where the Hebrew has "the sons of Hashem the Gizonite"), along with readings such as "son of Nathan" (11:38), "the son of Zeruiah" without "Joab" (11:39), and "Josiah his son, Ellaam" (11:46).
notes.12:1: Greek reads "Sokla" here and "Soglam" in 12:21, Septuagint forms corresponding to Hebrew "Ziklag." Several personal names in 12:3-14, 21, and 28 also preserve distinct Greek textual forms (such as Joel for Jeziel, Eliab for Eliel, Eliezer for Elzabad, and Toadas for Jehoiada).
notes.12:18: Greek "at one" renders the idiom kath' heauten ("by itself / in accord"), and "not in truth of hand" differs from the Hebrew ("with no violence in my hands").
notes.12:19: Greek reads "Go, and your people" (taking the Hebrew consonants as an imperative and "your people"), where the Hebrew has "Yours we are... and with you."
notes.12:22: Greek ton geddour ("the geddur") is an untranslated transliteration (with a d/r shift) of the Hebrew word for "the raiding band."
notes.12:34: Greek reads "not empty-handed" (Hebrew: "not with a double heart"); in 12:36, Greek reads "twenty-eight thousand eight hundred" (Hebrew: 28,600).
notes.13:6: Greek reads "David brought it up; and all Israel went up to the city of David," differing from the Hebrew ("David and all Israel went up to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim").
notes.13:7: Greek reads "Amminadab" (Hebrew: "Abinadab") and plural "his brothers" (Hebrew: "Ahio" or "his brother").
notes.13:9: Greek omits the name of the threshing floor (Hebrew: "Chidon") and reads "and the calf turned it aside" (Greek moschos, "calf," also in 12:41).
notes.13:13: Greek reads "Abeddara" (and "Abeddaram" in 13:14), a Septuagint form corresponding to Hebrew "Obed-edom."
notes.14:4: Several names of David's sons in 14:4-7 preserve distinct Septuagint forms (Isoboam, Baar, Ektae, Nageth, Naphath, Januu, Balegdae, and Emphalet) differing from the Hebrew list.
notes.14:8: Here and throughout 14:8-16 (as in 12:20), Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard rendering for the Philistines; in 14:9 and 14:13, "Valley of the Giants" translates Hebrew "Valley of Rephaim."
notes.14:11: Greek reads "Phaalphathisim" and "Breakthrough of Pharisin" for Hebrew "Baal-perazim," and omits an explicit subject "God" before "has broken through."
notes.14:14: Greek renders the trees as "pear trees" (Hebrew: balsam or mulberry trees) and in 14:15 reads "the sound of the shaking of the very tops" (Hebrew: "the sound of marching in the tops").
notes.15:2: The Greek text lacks the phrase "to carry the ark of the Lord" found in the Hebrew, reading literally "for the Lord chose them also to minister to Him forever."
notes.15:5: In verses 5-7, the Greek gives distinct totals for three Levitical clans (one hundred ten, two hundred fifty, and one hundred fifty) compared with the Hebrew (one hundred twenty, two hundred twenty, and one hundred thirty), and in verses 8-11 preserves distinct name forms (Elisaphat, Ener, Ariel, and Enel).
notes.15:18: In verses 18-21, the Greek preserves several distinct name forms compared with the Hebrew (Uzziel, Elioel, Eliphena, Makelleiah, Uzziah, Eithel, and Enphanaias); in verse 21, "amasenith" transliterates the musical term corresponding to Hebrew "hasheminith," and "to be strong" reflects a distinct Greek rendering of the Hebrew musical direction.
notes.15:26: The Greek uses the distributive expression "seven ... each" for the sacrifices, and renders Hebrew "bulls" with "calves."
notes.15:27: The Greek reads "Jeconiah" rather than "Chenaniah" (as in verse 22 and the Hebrew) and repeats "a robe of fine linen" at the end of the verse rather than mentioning a linen ephod.
notes.16:3: Greek "amoreiten" (a spelling of "amorites") denotes a sweet honey cake; the Greek lists two food items rather than the three found in the Hebrew.
notes.16:23: The Greek critical text omits verse 24, moving directly from verse 23 to verse 25, and likewise lacks the opening clause of verse 29 found in the Hebrew.
notes.16:28: The Greek text reads "Father of the nations" ("patri ton ethnon") rather than "families of the nations" ("patriai ton ethnon") found in the Hebrew and other Greek witnesses.
notes.16:32: Greek "bobbesei" (a spelling of "bombesei," "will roar") is future indicative, and "the tree of the field" lacks a separate verb where the Hebrew reads "let the field exult."
notes.16:35: The Greek reads past-tense "has saved us" rather than the imperative "Save us" of the Hebrew; similarly, verse 34 has neuter "for it is good," and verse 36 omits "and to everlasting" and uses future "will say."
notes.16:39: The Greek transliterates Hebrew "bamah" ("high place") as a proper place name, "Bama, which is in Gibeon"; in verse 40, the Greek adds "by the hand of Moses, the servant of God."
notes.17:6: The Greek reads "one tribe of Israel" (where the Hebrew has "any of the judges of Israel") and omits "whom I commanded" before "to shepherd My people."
notes.17:10: The Greek reads "I will increase you, and the Lord will build you," whereas the Hebrew reads "I declare to you that the Lord will build a house for you."
notes.17:11: "from your body" translates Greek ek tes koilias sou (literally "from your belly"), whereas the Hebrew has "from your sons."
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "that You have loved me forever," differing from the Hebrew "that You have brought me thus far."
notes.17:17: "as a vision of a man, and You have exalted me" renders the Greek reading of a difficult Hebrew clause; similarly in 17:23-24 the Greek omits two clauses present in the Hebrew and transitions directly into "as they say."
notes.18:1: "the foreigners" translates Greek allophyloi (literally "people of another tribe"), the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines (also in 18:11).
notes.18:7: "collars" renders Greek kloioi (neckbands or collars), where the Hebrew has "shields"; similarly in 18:4 the Greek reads "seven thousand horses" rather than "horsemen."
notes.18:8: "Metabechas" is a Septuagint-distinct name reflecting Hebrew "from Tibhath," and "the chosen wars" translates Greek ton eklekton polemon (where the Hebrew has "from Cun, cities of Hadarezer").
notes.18:9: "Thoa" is the Septuagint form corresponding to Hebrew Tou (also in 18:10); in 18:11-13 "Idumea" and "Idumeans" render Greek Idoumaia/Idoumaioi (Hebrew Edom), and 18:13 places the garrisons "in the valley" rather than "in Edom."
notes.18:17: The Greek reads "over the priests and Phalteia" (a Septuagint-distinct name) where the Hebrew has "over the Cherethites and the Pelethites"; likewise in 18:15-16 the Greek names "Ahijah" (for Hebrew Ahilud) and "Joshua" (for Hebrew Shavsha).
notes.19:2: "Hanan" (also in 19:1, 3, 4, 6) and "Hanas" are Septuagint-distinct forms corresponding to Hebrew Hanun and Nahash (whose name is absent in the Greek of 19:1).
notes.19:4: "up to the fold" translates Greek heos tes anaboles (the fold or drape of a garment), rendering a rare Hebrew term meaning "hips" or "buttocks"; in 19:3 the Greek likewise reads "search out the city" where the Hebrew has "search and overthrow."
notes.19:6: The Greek reads "that the people of David had been put to shame" (where the Hebrew has "that they had made themselves odious to David") and names "Sobal" (distinct from Zobah in chapter 18).
notes.19:13: The Greek text here is much shorter than the Hebrew, omitting Joab's exhortation to be strong and courageous for the people and cities of God.
notes.19:16: "Sophar" (and "Saphath" in 19:18) are Septuagint-distinct forms corresponding to Hebrew Shophach.
notes.20:2: Greek reads "Molchol their king," a proper-name rendering corresponding to Hebrew Milcom (or "their king").
notes.20:3: Greek explicitly uses dieprisen ("sawed apart") with only two tools ("saws" and "iron adzes") and reads tois paisin ("the servants"), likely an early scribal variant for pasin ("all"), where Hebrew has "all the cities of the sons of Ammon."
notes.20:4: Greek allophyloi literally means "foreigners" (the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines); the Greek forms "Thosathi" and "Saphut" correspond to Hebrew "the Hushathite" and "Sippai," and the final verb is singular active ("humbled him").
notes.20:5: The Greek names "Ellan" and "Elemee" correspond to Hebrew "Elhanan" and "Lahmi."
notes.20:8: Greek reads the singular "this one" and adds "all of them were four giants" (compare 2 Samuel 21:22), a clause absent from the Hebrew of 1 Chronicles 20:8.
notes.21:1: Greek diabolos lacks the definite article and can mean "an adversary/accuser" or "the devil" (rendering Hebrew satan); Greek also reads "in Israel" rather than "against Israel."
notes.21:4: The Greek text is much shorter than the Hebrew, omitting Joab's departure and tour through Israel; the Hebrew clause "the king's word prevailed over Joab" appears instead in verse 6 (replacing Hebrew "was abhorrent to Joab"), and verse 5 omits the separate count for Judah.
notes.21:20: Greek reads "the king" (Hebrew "the angel") and leaves the Hebrew participle mithabbeim ("hiding themselves") untranslated as methachabein.
notes.21:26: The final clause "and consumed the burnt offering" is a Septuagint addition not present in the Hebrew text.
notes.21:30: Greek ou katespeusen ("did not hasten") differs from Hebrew "was terrified"; in verse 29 Greek also transliterates Hebrew bamah ("high place") as the place name "Bamoth."
notes.22:2: Greek proselytoi ("proselytes") is the Septuagint's standard equivalent for Hebrew gerim ("resident aliens").
notes.22:11: Here and in verse 13, Greek uses the third-person future active euodosei ("He will grant success") with the Lord as subject, whereas the Hebrew has second-person forms ("you will succeed").
notes.22:15: Greek includes the imperative prosthes ("add"), echoing the end of verse 14 and not present in the Hebrew.
notes.22:17: Greek reads tois paisin ("the servants"), likely an early scribal variant for pasin ("all"), as in 20:3; in verse 18 Greek has plural en chersin ("into your hands," without an explicit possessive pronoun) where Hebrew reads "into my hand."
notes.23:3: The Greek text reads the active verb 'counted' (rather than passive 'were counted') with the Levites as subject.
notes.23:5: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek text omits the four thousand gatekeepers (leaving the itemized figures totaling thirty-four thousand rather than thirty-eight thousand) and uses the third-person verb 'he made' rather than first-person 'I made.'
notes.23:7: The Greek text reads the distinct names Parosom (for Hebrew 'the Gershonites') and Edan (for Hebrew Ladan, reading the initial consonant as a preposition).
notes.23:9: Across this chapter's genealogies the Greek text preserves distinctive names differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text: Alothim, Hieiel, and Haidan (v. 9), Joash (vv. 10-11), Idud, Amadiah, Uzziel, and Ikemias (v. 19), and Aidath and Arimoth (v. 23); in vv. 8-9 'and three' runs across the verse division into the sons of Shimei.
notes.23:28: Greek epi cheira Aaron literally reads "at the hand of Aaron," an idiom meaning "at the side of / assisting the line of Aaron."
notes.23:32: The Greek text lists only two charges here, omitting 'the charge of the sanctuary' found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; earlier in v. 28 it similarly reads 'at the hand of Aaron' and 'the service of God' without 'sons of' and 'house of.'
notes.24:4: The Greek text inserts 'Aaron' before 'Ithamar' and omits the number 'eight' for Ithamar's paternal houses, while in v. 6 it reads 'one by one' (reflecting Hebrew 'one' rather than Masoretic 'taken').
notes.24:14: The Greek text omits the fourteenth course of the Hebrew list (Jeshebeab; Gelba corresponds to Bilgah), shifting the remaining courses so that the list ends at twenty-three rather than twenty-four (v. 18); across vv. 7-18 it also preserves distinctive Greek name forms (Jarim, Anaidiah, Hareb, Benjamin, Ischaniah, Eliabiei, Hocchoppha, Gelba, Hezin, Aphese, Achim, Adallai, and Maasai).
notes.24:21: The Greek text omits the name of Rehabiah's son (Isshiah in the Hebrew Masoretic Text), reading simply 'for Rehabiah, the chief,' and similarly in v. 20 omits 'for the sons of Shubael' and reads Jobael.
notes.24:28: The Greek text adds 'and Ithamar' and 'and Eleazar died' (neither in the Hebrew Masoretic Text), and across vv. 22-30 preserves distinctive Greek name forms: Inath (v. 22), Jedimu, Amadiah, Jase, and Jokom (v. 23, omitting Hebron), Uzziah (vv. 26-27), Isoam and Abai (v. 27), and Elah and Arimoth (v. 30).
notes.24:31: The Greek text omits 'David' after 'the king,' uses singular 'chief,' and renders the Hebrew 'ancestral houses of the head' as 'the patriarchs of Araab,' followed by 'just as his younger brothers.'
notes.25:1: The Greek 'who spoke out' (apophthengomenous) denotes solemn or inspired utterance (where the Hebrew has 'prophesied'), and 'head by head' preserves a Septuagint-distinct reading.
notes.25:2: Sacchus, Nathalias, and Erael are Septuagint-distinct name forms corresponding to Zaccur, Nethaniah, and Asharelah in the Hebrew text.
notes.25:3: Tuna and Saia are Septuagint-distinct forms (for Hebrew Gedaliah and Jeshaiah), and the Greek includes Shimei to reach the stated total of six; 'sounding forth' (anakrouomenos) literally means striking up a stringed instrument (also in v. 5).
notes.25:4: The Greek lists Azarel (Hebrew: Uzziel), adds Amsu while omitting Hanani, and renders the closing names with Septuagint-distinct forms (Romei, 'the sons of Od,' Jeibasaka, Manthei, and Melzoth) corresponding to Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, and Mahazioth.
notes.25:9: Galuia and Heneia reflect a Septuagint-distinct rendering of Hebrew Gedaliah and 'he'; across vv. 10-31, Zacchuth, Nathan, Jeseriel, Josiah, Emei, Azariah, Haria, Bakata, Hananiah (v. 25), Methathei, Aematha, Hethei, Godomathei, and Romelchei preserve the Greek forms (and v. 10 reads singular 'his son').
notes.26:1: The Greek reads 'of the gates' (also in v. 12, vs. 'gatekeepers' in v. 19), renders Meshelemiah as Mosolael (and as Mosalea in v. 2, Mosomameid in v. 9), and divides Hebrew Asaph/Ebiasaph into 'from the sons of Abijah, Saphar.'
notes.26:2: The Greek syntax reads 'as for Mosalea, son of Zechariah' and omits the ordinals through the sixth, while vv. 2-7 preserve Septuagint-distinct names (Iderel, Zechariah, Jenonel, Jolam, Jonah; Joath, Naas, Jehiel, Japhthoslaathi; 'the firstborn Rosai'; Goonei, Ahihud, Ennu, Sabchia, and Isbakom).
notes.26:10: The Greek translates Hebrew 'Shimri the chief' as 'keeping the leadership' and 'Hilkiah the second' as 'of the second division,' followed by the distinct form Tablai in v. 11.
notes.26:14: Soaz and Malchiah preserve Septuagint-distinct names where the Hebrew describes Zechariah as a prudent counselor; in vv. 15-18, Esephin/Esephim transliterates the Hebrew term for storehouses, and v. 18 preserves the expanded Greek repetition (including both three and four guards on the west).
notes.26:21: Several Septuagint-distinct readings appear across vv. 19-31: Kohath (v. 19), 'their brothers' (v. 20), Chadan and 'Jaieel son of Jehu' (v. 21), Joel (v. 24), Hoshaiah (v. 25), 'from cities' (v. 27, Greek poleon vs. polemon 'wars'), and Tudeias with singular 'a mighty man' in Riazer (v. 31).
notes.27:1: Greek reads "who served the people," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "who served the king."
notes.27:2: Throughout vv. 2-15 the Greek preserves several distinct names compared with the Hebrew: Sobal (v. 2; Heb. Jashobeam), Dodai the Ekchoch (v. 4; Heb. the Ahohite), Laibazath (v. 6; Heb. Ammizabad), Salaoth the Ezrahite (v. 8; Heb. Shamhuth the Izrahite), Hodaviah (v. 9, Greek Odouias; Heb. Ira), and Chesles from Phallous (v. 10; Heb. Helez the Pelonite). Also in v. 4 the Greek ends with "leaders of the army" and lacks the Hebrew reference to Mikloth.
notes.27:7: Greek reads "Obadiah" (Abdeias) and "and the brothers," whereas the Hebrew reads "Zebadiah" and "after him."
notes.27:17: In the tribal list (vv. 17-22) the Greek differs from the Hebrew on several names: Samuel (v. 17; Heb. Kemuel), Eliab and Mishael (v. 18; Heb. Elihu and Michael), Shemaiah (v. 19; Heb. Ishmaiah), Uzziah and Phaladaia (v. 20; Heb. Azaziah and Pedaiah), Jaddai, Zabdiah, and Asier (v. 21; Heb. Iddo, Zechariah, and Jaasiel), and Joram (v. 22; Heb. Jeroham).
notes.27:27: Greek reads "estates" (choria) rather than Hebrew "vineyards," and in vv. 26-32 preserves several distinct names: Chobud (v. 26; Heb. Chelub), Rael, Zichri, and the son of Sephni (v. 27; Heb. the Ramathite, Zabdi, and the Shiphmite), Asidon, Asartais, Sophan, and Adai (v. 29; Heb. Sharon, Shitrai, Shaphat, and Adlai), Abijah and Merathon (v. 30; Heb. Obil and the Meronothite), the Garite (v. 31; Heb. the Hagrite), and Hachami (v. 32; Heb. Hachmoni).
notes.27:33: Greek calls Hushai "the first friend of the king," reflecting a Hellenistic court title rather than the Hebrew gentilic "the Archite." In v. 34 the compressed Greek wording "after this Ahithophel, coming next" identifies those who succeeded Ahithophel as royal counselors.
notes.28:1: Greek reads "leaders of the judges" (reflecting Hebrew shoftim) rather than "leaders of the tribes" (shevatim), and renders the royal attendants with the Hellenistic phrase "around the king's person."
notes.28:2: Greek reads "of our Lord" (kyriou hemon) rather than Hebrew "of our God," and "the things needed for the dwelling place" rather than "preparations to build."
notes.28:6: Greek reads "will inherit My house and My court" (singular) rather than Hebrew "shall build My house and My courts." In v. 8 the Greek text is shorter than the Hebrew and reads "for our sons" (first-person plural) rather than "for your sons."
notes.28:11: "Zakcho" (and "sakcho" in v. 20) is an untranslated Greek transliteration of a rare Hebrew loanword (ganzak) meaning treasuries or storerooms. Also in v. 11 Greek reads "of the temple" rather than Hebrew "of the porch," and in vv. 14-15 the Greek text is substantially shorter than the Hebrew.
notes.28:19: Unlike the Hebrew, which shifts into first-person speech from David, the Greek keeps v. 19 in third-person narrative ("David gave to Solomon"). In v. 20 the Greek adds a distinctive recapitulation of the temple plan from vv. 11-12 at the end of David's charge.
notes.29:2: Greek soom transliterates Hebrew shoham (commonly identified as onyx or carnelian), and parion denotes Parian marble from the island of Paros where the Hebrew text refers to alabaster or marble.
notes.29:4: Suphir (Greek Soupheir) is the Septuagint form of the place name corresponding to Ophir in the Hebrew text.
notes.29:8: Besiel the Gersomnite (Greek Besiel tou Gersomnei) is the Septuagint name corresponding to Jehiel the Gershonite in the Hebrew text.
notes.29:11: The Greek text reads nominative "You, Lord, are..." rather than "Yours is...", supplies the verb "hold dominion", and ends with "before Your face every king and nation is shaken" where the Hebrew text speaks of God's kingdom and headship over all.
notes.29:30: The Greek text lacks the noun "times" before the plural relative pronoun "which" and includes the closing sentence concerning Solomon, which corresponds to 2 Chronicles 1:1 in the Hebrew text.
